authoring_rules: Fifth held-out set (TypeScript, one repository), for two pre-registered checks: the test-file exclusion from natural-language search, and the shipped summary field (w = 0.5) on a repository whose API is written as `export const f = () => {}`.
honojs/hono was dropped from set 4 because PRISM did not index const-bound functions; written after that parser fix (3cd55ed), against its candidate pool with test files excluded.

Written from the source at the pinned commit before any engine, search, ranking or summarizer ran on it. Only a name-only index (candidate pool names) was built, to check that gold and decoys are candidates.
Same rules as sets 1-4: developer phrasing; gold = the function(s) that directly answer; decoys = plausible wrong functions (same stems, the inverse operation, the caller or the helper).
No question contains its gold symbol's name or every word of it (checked by check.py).
Gold and decoys are library code, never test or type-test files. 27 of the 32 gold symbols are const-bound functions that had no symbol before the parser fix.

questions.question: How is the path portion pulled out of an incoming request's address without building a full URL object, and when are percent escapes decoded?
How is a route that ends in an optional parameter, like /animals/:type?, expanded into the concrete routes it stands for?
How are a base path and a sub path joined so that exactly one slash separates them?
How is one value looked up in the query string without parsing all of it, and what comes back when the key is present without an '='?
When a GET for an address ending in a slash finds nothing, how is the client redirected to the same address without the slash?
Which response headers let a browser on another site call this API, and how is the allowed origin chosen when a list or a callback is configured?
How are form submissions coming from other sites rejected, using the Sec-Fetch-Site header first and the Origin header otherwise?
How is an upload larger than allowed refused, both when its size is declared up front and when it arrives in chunks?
How does the server answer 304 Not Modified when the client already holds the current version of a response, and which headers survive on that reply?
How are allow and deny rules written as address ranges in CIDR notation turned into a fast check of the caller's IP?
How is a shortened IPv6 address with '::', or one ending in an IPv4 part, written out as eight full groups?
How are the username and password recovered from the credentials header a client sends with the Basic scheme?
How does the token check answer a missing header, a malformed header and a wrong token differently, and what does it put in WWW-Authenticate?
How is a handler cut off with an error when it runs longer than a configured number of milliseconds?
How can an HTML form that only sends POST be turned into a PUT or DELETE, using a hidden field, a header or a query parameter?
Which naming rules must a Set-Cookie value satisfy for the __Secure- and __Host- prefixes, and how long may it live before it is refused?
How are tamper-proof cookies read back, keeping only values whose HMAC matches and marking the others as invalid?
When a token is checked, how are its not-before, expiry, issued-at and issuer claims enforced before the signature is tested?
How are two secrets compared without leaking how many characters matched through the time it takes?
How are form fields with dotted names like user.address.city turned into nested objects in the parsed request body?
When several entries of an Accept-style header carry the same weight, in which order are they returned?
When several router implementations are configured, how is the first one able to take every registered route picked, and how do later requests skip that choice?
How does the middleware chain run each handler in order, send thrown errors to the error handler, and stop a handler from advancing twice?
How is a separate application's fetch handler attached under a path prefix, with the prefix stripped before the request is passed on?
How is one server-sent event put on the wire, including the event name, id and retry fields and data spanning several lines?
Which conditions stop a response from being gzip-encoded, and how is the encoding picked from what the client accepts?
When a request is forwarded to another server, which connection-specific headers are dropped from the copy that is sent?
How is a named duration added to the Server-Timing header, with or without a description and a precision?
How are the characters that are special in HTML replaced while text is appended to the output buffer?
How is the visitor's preferred language taken from the Accept-Language header, falling through the listed languages until a supported one is found?
